name: e10_costs
title: 10. Execution and cost realism: does friction change the verdict?
text:
**Question.** Are the default frictions (5 bp per side, 15 bp for Bitcoin, next-close fills) realistic, and would different costs or fill timing change any conclusion?

**Setup.** Spreads are estimated from daily highs and lows with Corwin & Schultz (2012); EMA50/200 is re-run with flat costs of 0, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 bp per side; break-even costs are solved exactly (arithmetic edge / turnover) and by root-finding full backtests; and every asset is re-run with same-close, next-open and next-close fills.

**Findings.**

- The robust Corwin-Schultz estimate (window averages clipped at zero) is essentially zero for 6 of 11 exchange-traded assets; the paper's baseline (two-day estimates clipped at zero) gives an upward-biased median 26 bp (24 bp over the last 5 years). The one-tick spread at the latest price is a median 0.96 bp (widest: DBC, 2.96 bp), so the assumed 2 bp half-spread is at least half a tick for every US-listed asset at today's prices, and the 5 bp all-in cost per side is generous for those that quote at one tick. That is not a safe bound for the early sample: before decimalisation (2001) US shares were quoted in fractions of a dollar and relative spreads were wider. Bitcoin: 4 bp robust, 85 bp daily-clipped.
- The rule trades a median 0.67 round trips a year, so the default costs drag returns by a median 7 bp a year (most: BTC-USD, 23 bp).
- Raising costs from 0 to 20 bp per side lowers Sharpe by at most 0.017 across SPY, QQQ, GLD, BTC-USD, NVDA; even 100 bp lowers it by at most 0.09.
- Measured against T-bills, the arithmetic edge disappears only at 101 bp per side for the weakest asset (TLT; median 381 bp). Against buy-and-hold the rule's CAGR is higher even at zero cost in only 3 of 12 assets (QQQ up to 180 bp; IEF up to 12 bp; DBC up to 67 bp); its Sharpe is higher in 6 of 12, an advantage that survives to a median 102 bp per side (lowest: IEF, 27 bp).
- Same-close instead of next-close fills changes the 50/200 Sharpe by a median -0.007 (range -0.026 to +0.026; CAGR -11 bp a year); next-open fills by -0.002. For a fast EMA5/20 rule the mean absolute same-close effect is 0.072 Sharpe vs 0.014 for 50/200, several times larger, but its median is +0.012: noise around zero rather than a systematic gain. On the notebook's own NVDA 2022-2024 window, same-close fills give +290% total return vs +322% for next-close (Sharpe 1.13 vs 1.19).

**Interpretation.** A slow trend rule is a low-turnover strategy: with under one round trip a year, costs scale with a handful of trades, not with the holding period, so realistic friction is not what makes it trail buy-and-hold on CAGR in most markets; the verdict is set by the signal. The exception is IEF, where the comparison with buy-and-hold is close enough that a cost within 4x the default flips it. This matches the finding that trend-following returns survive estimated trading costs (Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen 2017), and a 50/200 rule trades far less than their 1-12 month signals. The daily-bar spread estimates are bounds, not measurements: when the spread is a cent and daily volatility is a percent, the Corwin & Schultz (2012) estimator either collapses to zero or, clipped day by day, overstates the spread many times over. The same-close fill convention barely matters for a 50/200 rule: with about 1.3 position changes a year, the one-day difference touches roughly 13 days per decade, and on the notebook's own NVDA window it did not flatter the result either. Even for a fast rule its sign is unstable, consistent with daily returns that are, if anything, mildly mean-reverting (median lag-1 autocorrelation -0.043); whatever inflated the notebook's numbers (section 1), fill timing is at most a small part of it on full histories.
after: Costs are proportional and symmetric; market impact is ignored, which is reasonable for retail size in these ETFs but not for large orders in thinner products such as DBC or early Bitcoin. Crypto fees vary widely by venue and account tier. The break-even search is capped at 2,000 bp per side.
